fields.Front: Why build a reusable WCAG 2.1 TypeScript component library instead of styling each page individually?
fields.Back: It centralizes accessible, typed components so every new screen reuses tested, compliant building blocks instead of re-implementing accessibility per page — which is what drove the 30% faster frontend cycles.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Tell me about a performance problem you diagnosed and fixed."
fields.Back:
S: ServiceOntario's Spring Boot + React compliance workflows, used by 15M+ residents, had slow read paths.
T: Find and fix the root cause of the read-latency issue.
A: Diagnosed an N+1 query bottleneck, fixed it with JPQL JOIN FETCH to eagerly load associations in one query, and tuned Hibernate batch sizes for remaining lazy loads.
R: Read latency dropped 40%.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Tell me about a time you improved accessibility in a product."
fields.Back:
S: ServiceOntario's frontend needed to meet public-sector accessibility requirements while shipping features quickly.
T: Provide reusable, compliant UI building blocks for the team.
A: Built a WCAG 2.1-compliant TypeScript UI component library.
R: Frontend development cycles got 30% faster since teams reused accessible components instead of building them from scratch.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Walk me through a full-stack project you worked on at scale."
fields.Back:
S: ServiceOntario needed compliance workflows serving 15M+ residents.
T: Contribute full-stack, from backend performance to frontend accessibility.
A: Worked across a Spring Boot + React stack — fixed an N+1 bottleneck with JOIN FETCH and Hibernate batch tuning, and built a WCAG 2.1 TypeScript UI library.
R: 40% lower read latency and 30% faster frontend cycles, on a system serving 15M+ residents.

fields.Text: At ServiceOntario, Michele fixed N+1 query bottlenecks using JPQL {{c1::JOIN FETCH}} and tuned {{c2::Hibernate batch sizes}}, achieving {{c3::40%}} lower read latency.

fields.Back: A performance bug where fetching a list of N records triggers one additional query per record (N extra queries) instead of a single batched/joined query.
A JPQL clause that eagerly loads an associated entity or collection within the same query, avoiding the extra per-row queries that cause N+1 problems.
